payload.reason: The evidence provides a clear description of how crowd workers were instructed to identify important elements in document collections using a novel crowdsourcing scheme.

claims.text: Crowd workers were instructed to provide importance scores for propositions related to document clusters without reading the documents, using only a description of the topic and the propositions themselves.
The crowdsourcing scheme employed a 5-point Likert scale for workers to rate the importance of propositions, allowing for more nuanced annotations.
The approach aimed to simplify tasks for workers, making them small and quick to complete, which improved efficiency and scalability compared to traditional methods.
